newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

The strong tone to boxed beef and fed cattle markets was expected to encourage renewed buying in live cattle futures. Futures had slipped late Tuesday on profit taking and commercial hedge selling but are expected to firm again with beef prices at five-week highs, analysts said.
The value of heavy-weight choice boxed beef ran up to $105.33 per cwt Tuesday, a $2.49 jump since Monday's close and the highest level since March 10.

Feeder cattle futures were also expected to show strength despite late profit-taking Tuesday. Renewed buying was expected to stem from a higher CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures indications, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.17 to $70.65 per cwt.
However, trade could turn uneven as traders look ahead to Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, they said.

Estimates for the number of cattle on feed in large feedlots in the seven major states ranged from 106 to 108 percent of a year ago. Placements ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent and marketings 98 to 104.5 percent.
